paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens across different medical specialties, comparing a baseline model (Mistralv0.2-Base) to versions fine-tuned on data from each specialty. The horizontal axis lists six specialty groups: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, in a categorical scale without a specific order. The vertical axis represents negative log probability, labeled with a linear scale ranging from -27 to -22, with tick labels at regular intervals of 1 unit. Within each specialty group, there are bars representing Mistralv0.2-Base and five fine-tuned models, each colored differently according to a legend: Cardio (light orange), Gastro (orange), Infect (dark orange), Neuro (brown), Obstetrics (dark brown), and Pediatrics (black). The Mistralv0.2-Base bar in light blue consistently appears at the top of each group, with a value ranging from approximately -22.5 to -23.5 across the groups. The fine-tuned model bars within each group show varying heights, with Gastro and Infect models often appearing among the lowest, indicating higher negative log probabilities. Notably, the Infect group has the largest overall bar heights, while the Cardio group shows the smallest spread between the baseline and fine-tuned variants. No bars are explicitly sorted, emphasized, or annotated beyond their color coding and positioning within each group.
